subject: HC request: runtime & platform headcount rebalance + comp-band exception
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: reallocate runtime HC to US + comp-band exception for Sr Runtime Eng

Hi team,

Quick ask ahead of next week's capacity check: the runtime hiring plan needs a small but time-sensitive update. We have an open, budgeted FTE currently tagged to EMEA (slot: Runtime Engineer II) that the infra roadmap indicates would have materially slower time-to-productivity for our low-latency initiatives in Q1 if it remains remote/EMEA-assigned.

Proposal (two parts):
- Reclassify that single EMEA slot to a US-based Senior Runtime Engineer (band exception required — target is to hire at the top of Senior band to land strong candidates).
- Approve a 10% comp-band exception for this hire (one-off, justified by market/criticality).

Why: we have a near-term customer POC (low-latency caching) that must show sub-30ms 95th percentile before contract signature. That requires senior hands-on kernel/ops expertise and proximity to our US test infra. Candidate pipeline: Greenwood has two candidates who can start Dec/Jan. Without the reclass, we would either push the POC or accept a less-experienced hire and take more risk.

Attachments: comp-band-appendix.pdf (market comps), hc-heatmap-q4.xlsx (roster heatmap and cost delta), candidate-pricing-summary.pdf (Greenwood summary).

Ask: please sign off or send me questions by EOD Monday. If you want a short sync I can join — 15 minutes should suffice.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Platform Hiring
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the clear ask. A couple of quick clarifying questions before I can +1: 
1) Headcount budget impact: what is the incremental OTE cost vs current budget for the slot (annualized)? The heatmap shows a delta but I want the explicit line item.
2) Timeline risk: if we keep the EMEA slot, how long until a comparable candidate is ready (estimate in weeks)?
3) Internal mobility possibility: is there a near-term internal candidate in US who could fill without a band exception?

If Greenwood already has strong screened candidates and the delta is within the submitted heatmap, I'm inclined to approve — but need the numbers so FP&A can reconcile.

If it's easier, loop me into Greenwood's candidate briefs and I'll skim.

—Kim
Kimberly Park

Kim, Marissa —

Following up with the line-item numbers you requested. Summary below and attaching the candidate pricing PDF (candidate-pricing-summary.pdf).

- Current budgeted slot (EMEA Runtime II): fully loaded annual = $185,000
- Proposed US Senior Runtime (adjusted for band exception): fully loaded annual = $235,000
- Delta (annual): $50,000 (one slot) — roughly 27% uplift to headcount line.
- Estimated ramp / time to productivity: Senior hire onsite/US -> 6–8 weeks to be contributing on kernel/infra projects vs 10–14 weeks for mid-level EMEA hire (depends on interview-to-offer cadence).
- Greenwood pipeline: 2 active candidates, both have kernel-level system experience, one has prior low-latency infra experience at a trading/edge company. Estimated start date if offer accepted and notice given: mid-Dec to early Jan.

Internal mobility check: Karthik reports two potential internal applicants but both are early in their ramp and would not meet the 6–8 week productivity target.

Recommendation: Approve the reclass + 10% comp-band exception as a targeted one-off for Q4 hiring. The customer POC risk and potential revenue acceleration justify the delta; hiring now is cheaper than delaying the contract by a quarter.

Soojin Lee
Talent Partner, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment: candidate-pricing-summary.pdf
